units.text: INT. PRINTING SHOP, MANCHESTER - EVENING (1838)
Ink-black presses.
Racks of lead type.
A single tallow candle gutters beside a chalkboard of tomorrow's handbills.
EZEKIEL FARTHING, thirties, compositor, in a leather apron, sets type with quick, practised fingers.
Ink stains him to the elbow.
A knock.
The door opens, letting in cold and the smell of coal smoke.
PRUDENCE ASHWORTH, twenties, a mill-girl in a patched shawl, steps in clutching a folded paper.
Mr. Farthing? They said you'd print for a penny.
units.name: PRUDENCE

units.text: Depends what it says.
units.name: EZEKIEL

units.text: It says we want ten hours. No more.
units.name: PRUDENCE

units.text: Who is "we"?
units.name: EZEKIEL

units.text: The women at Greaves Mill. All three hundred.
units.name: PRUDENCE

units.text: And who signs it?
units.name: EZEKIEL

units.text: Nobody. That's the point. If nobody signs it, nobody's turned out.
units.name: PRUDENCE

units.text: Ezekiel wipes his hands on his apron.
He takes the paper and reads it by the candle.
His lips move.
It's a good bill.
units.name: EZEKIEL

units.text: Will you print it?
units.name: PRUDENCE

units.text: I'll print it. Come back Thursday.
units.name: EZEKIEL

units.text: Thursday's too late. The vote is tomorrow.
units.name: PRUDENCE

units.text: Then I'd best set it tonight.
units.name: EZEKIEL
